name: David
summary: Israel's aging king; on his deathbed he secures Solomon's succession and charges him to walk faithfully with God and settle old scores.

name: Solomon
summary: David's son who becomes king, asks God for wisdom instead of wealth, builds the temple, and whose later foreign wives and idolatry lead the LORD to tear the kingdom from his son.

name: Adonijah
summary: David's son who declares himself king while David is still alive; Solomon spares him once but later has him executed for requesting Abishag as a wife.

name: Joab
summary: David's longtime army commander who backs Adonijah's claim to the throne; Solomon has Benaiah execute him at the altar for his earlier killings of Abner and Amasa.

name: Abiathar
summary: A priest who supports Adonijah's claim to the throne; Solomon exiles him from the priesthood rather than executing him, ending his family's priestly line.

name: Nathan
summary: The prophet who alerts Bathsheba to Adonijah's claim and helps persuade David to make Solomon king instead.

name: Bathsheba
summary: Solomon's mother; she appeals to David to keep his oath that Solomon would be king, and later unwittingly relays Adonijah's fatal request for Abishag.

name: Zadok
summary: A priest loyal to Solomon who anoints him king at Gihon and later replaces Abiathar as high priest.

name: Benaiah
summary: A loyal officer who helps anoint Solomon king, then executes Adonijah, Joab, and Shimei on Solomon's orders and becomes his army commander.

name: Shimei
summary: A man who once cursed David; Solomon confines him to Jerusalem under threat of death, then executes him three years later when he leaves the city.

name: Abishag
summary: A young woman brought to care for the aging David; Adonijah's request to marry her after David's death leads Solomon to have him executed.

name: The Boy's True Mother
summary: One of two women who claim the same surviving infant before Solomon; her plea to spare the child rather than divide him reveals she is his real mother.

name: Hiram of Tyre
summary: The king of Tyre who supplies Solomon with cedar and cypress timber for the temple in exchange for grain and oil, and later cities and sailors.

name: Hiram the Bronze Craftsman
summary: A skilled bronze worker from Tyre, distinct from King Hiram, whom Solomon brings in to cast the temple's pillars, the bronze sea, and other bronze furnishings.

name: The Queen of Sheba
summary: A foreign queen who travels to Jerusalem to test Solomon with hard questions and is overwhelmed by his wisdom and wealth.

name: Jeroboam
summary: A capable official of Solomon who becomes his adversary; the prophet Ahijah promises him ten tribes, and he becomes the first king of the divided northern kingdom, setting up golden calves at Bethel and Dan.

name: Ahijah
summary: A prophet who tears his cloak into twelve pieces to promise Jeroboam ten tribes, and who later, now blind, pronounces judgment on Jeroboam's house.

name: Rehoboam
summary: Solomon's son who becomes king of Judah; his harsh answer to Israel at Shechem splits the kingdom, and Egypt's Shishak later plunders Jerusalem during his reign.

name: The Man of God from Judah
summary: An unnamed prophet who confronts Jeroboam's altar at Bethel; he is later deceived into disobeying the LORD's command and is killed by a lion on the road.

name: The Old Prophet of Bethel
summary: An aging prophet living in Bethel who falsely claims an angel told him to feed the man of God from Judah, leading to the younger prophet's death.

name: Jeroboam's Wife
summary: Jeroboam's unnamed wife, sent in disguise to ask the prophet Ahijah about their sick son; he recognizes her anyway and pronounces judgment on the family.

name: Asa
summary: A king of Judah who removes his grandmother Maacah for making an idol and reforms the kingdom, though he later allies with Syria against Israel.

name: Baasha
summary: A king of Israel who assassinates Nadab and wipes out Jeroboam's entire family, fulfilling Ahijah's prophecy, before his own house is later condemned in turn.

name: Nadab
summary: Jeroboam's son and successor as king of Israel; he is assassinated by Baasha after a brief reign.

name: Elah
summary: Baasha's son and successor as king of Israel; he is assassinated by Zimri while drinking.

name: Zimri
summary: An officer who assassinates Elah and seizes the throne, but reigns only seven days before burning the palace down around himself when Omri is made king instead.

name: Omri
summary: A king of Israel who outlasts his rivals for the throne and builds Samaria as the kingdom's new capital; the text calls him more evil than every king before him.

name: Ahab
summary: Omri's son and king of Israel; he marries Jezebel and promotes Baal worship, clashes repeatedly with Elijah, takes Naboth's vineyard by murder, and dies in battle at Ramoth-gilead.

name: Jezebel
summary: Ahab's Phoenician wife who promotes Baal worship, purges the LORD's prophets, threatens Elijah's life, and arranges Naboth's murder to seize his vineyard for Ahab.

name: Elijah
summary: A prophet from Tishbe who announces a drought, is fed by ravens and a widow, defeats the prophets of Baal on Mount Carmel, hears the LORD in a low whisper at Horeb, and confronts Ahab over Naboth's murder.

name: Obadiah
summary: Ahab's official who secretly hides and feeds a hundred of the LORD's prophets during Jezebel's persecution.

name: Ben-hadad
summary: The king of Syria who besieges Samaria and is defeated by Ahab twice; Ahab spares his life, which an unnamed prophet condemns as a costly mercy.

name: Naboth
summary: A man of Jezreel who refuses to sell his family's vineyard to Ahab; Jezebel has him falsely accused and stoned to death so Ahab can take it.

name: Micaiah
summary: The one prophet who truthfully predicts Ahab's defeat at Ramoth-gilead against four hundred false prophets, and is imprisoned by Ahab for it.

name: Jehoshaphat
summary: The king of Judah who allies with Ahab against Syria, asks for Micaiah's true prophecy, and reigns righteously over Judah for twenty-five years.

name: Ahaziah
summary: Ahab and Jezebel's son who succeeds his father as king of Israel and continues his parents' worship of Baal.

name: Elisha
summary: A farmer whom Elijah calls as his successor by throwing his cloak over him; Elisha leaves his oxen behind to follow and serve him.

name: Hadad the Edomite
summary: A member of Edom's royal family who fled to Egypt as a boy when David conquered Edom, and whom the LORD raises up as an adversary against Solomon.

name: Rezon
summary: A man who becomes king of Damascus and opposes Israel throughout Solomon's reign, another adversary the LORD raises up against him.

name: The People of Israel
summary: The crowd gathered on Mount Carmel who fall on their faces and declare that the LORD is God once fire falls on Elijah's sacrifice.
